title: SR&ED & OIDMTC R&D Funding Documentation
description: From 2001 through 2025, I was the primary technical owner for Essential Skills' SR&ED and OIDMTC documentation. I helped prepare early claims, then took full ownership of the process before an external specialist was brought in. After outsourcing, I remained the technical point person: selecting qualifying projects, preparing first drafts, documenting technical uncertainty, experimentation and advancement, maintaining supporting evidence, and supplying the technical content used by the external firm.

sections.title: SR&ED Responsibility
paragraphs: I began helping with SR&ED documentation from 2001 to 2003 and took full ownership of the process from 2004 to 2009.
During that period I wrote the claims myself and was responsible for the complete technical documentation.

sections.title: Full Claim Ownership
paragraphs: I identified which development projects were appropriate to claim and wrote the technical narratives around the work.

sections.title: Engineering Financial Tracking
paragraphs: I was also involved in the financial side for the technical department so the claims could be supported by accurate engineering effort and cost information.

sections.title: External SR&ED Specialists
paragraphs: Around 2009, Essential Skills brought in an external specialist because preparing the claims was taking too much time away from software development.
The work was outsourced, but the technical ownership was not. I continued selecting the projects, preparing the initial technical drafts and working directly with the external firm.

sections.title: Primary Technical Contact
paragraphs: After the external firm became involved, I was their main technical point of contact through 2025.
I remained the primary source of the technical content while the outside specialists refined the submission and handled the broader filing process.

sections.title: OIDMTC
paragraphs: We also used Ontario Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit documentation when it was a better fit for the work than SR&ED.
For OIDMTC I identified the applicable projects and assembled the technical claims and supporting evidence, while the external firm handled the remaining filing paperwork.

sections.title: Choosing the Appropriate Program
paragraphs: Over the years we moved between SR&ED and OIDMTC depending on the nature of the work and which program best matched the qualifying development activity.

sections.title: Continuous Evidence Collection
paragraphs: I did not wait until filing time to reconstruct the history of a project. Supporting evidence was maintained continuously throughout development.
items: Weekly technical email logs sent to a dedicated SR&ED account

sections.title: Engineering Team Coordination
paragraphs: Before the external firm was involved, I worked with ownership and the development team to gather the information needed for each claim, but responsibility for producing the final technical submission rested with me.
After outsourcing, the technical relationship was primarily between me and the specialist firm, while ownership supplied the broader financial information they required.

sections.title: Claims & Reviews
paragraphs: The claims I prepared were accepted without significant difficulty.

Across the full period there were two government reviews/audits. The first occurred during the early years of the program, and another occurred much later on a relatively small claim prepared with the external firm. Both ultimately proceeded successfully.

sections.title: Broad R&D Coverage
paragraphs: The work covered a wide range of Essential Skills research and development efforts rather than a single product or technology.

Claims drew from software architecture, learning platforms, rendering and engine work, databases, cloud systems, authoring systems, web platforms and other areas where genuine technical uncertainty and experimental development occurred.

sections.title: R&D Leadership, Not Just Paperwork
paragraphs: The value of the work was not simply completing government forms. It required understanding the engineering deeply enough to identify genuine experimental development, distinguish routine implementation from technological uncertainty, preserve evidence, explain the work clearly, and connect months or years of development activity into a defensible technical narrative.

historicalNotes: The legacy portfolio card was titled 'Taxes and Grants' and significantly understated the duration and technical ownership of this work.
